title: Network performance

stations.name: Bandwidth
facts: Bandwidth is how much data can travel per second. The delay before data arrives is latency, a different factor.
Bandwidth is a rate, so it is measured in bits per second. Milliseconds measure latency; megabytes measure file size.

questions.a: The maximum amount of data that can be sent in a given time

questions.q: What unit is bandwidth usually measured in?

stations.name: Number of users
facts: The available bandwidth is split between everyone using it at that moment.
More bandwidth means each user's share is bigger, even when lots of people are online.

questions.q: Why does a network slow down when more people use it at the same time?
questions.a: They all share the same bandwidth, so each person gets less

questions.q: Which change would most help a network that is slow when everyone uses it at once?

stations.name: Transmission media
facts: Fibre carries data as light, with very high bandwidth over many kilometres.
Walls, distance and interference all weaken Wi-Fi. A cable delivers a steadier connection.

questions.q: Which connection usually offers the highest bandwidth over long distances?
Why is a wired connection usually more reliable than Wi-Fi?
questions.a: Wireless signals weaken with distance and are blocked by walls, but a cable isn't affected in the same way

stations.name: Error rate
facts: Resending damaged data uses extra bandwidth and time, so a high error rate slows everything down.
Other radio signals can interfere with Wi-Fi and damage data, so more of it has to be resent.

questions.q: What happens when a packet is damaged or lost on the way?
questions.a: It has to be sent again, which slows the network down

questions.q: Which is most likely to increase the error rate on a Wi-Fi network?
questions.a: Interference from other devices, such as microwave ovens and nearby Wi-Fi networks

stations.name: Latency
facts: Latency is a delay, measured in milliseconds. The amount of data per second is bandwidth.
In a game, every delay between pressing a button and seeing the result is noticeable. A download just needs to finish eventually.

questions.a: The delay between data being sent and it arriving

questions.q: For which activity does low latency matter most?

stations.name: Case study: CCTV
facts: Video is a lot of data. More cameras means more of the shared bandwidth is used up, all day and night.
Distance weakens Wi-Fi and increases errors. The manager should also check bandwidth and server storage for the extra video.

questions.q: Why could more CCTV cameras slow down the school network?
questions.a: Each camera streams video all the time, using up bandwidth that everyone shares

questions.q: The new cameras will be outside, a long way from the building. What is the best advice?
questions.a: Use cabled connections if possible, as Wi-Fi outdoors may be slow and unreliable, and check the network has enough bandwidth

final.name: Final challenge: diagnose the network

questions.q: Match each help desk problem to the factor causing it.
questions.a: Downloads slow right down every lunchtime, when 300 students go online → Number of users; A 10 Mbps connection can't stream several HD videos at once → Bandwidth; A laptop at the far end of the building keeps losing its Wi-Fi → Transmission media; Packets are corrupted near heavy machinery and keep being resent → Error rate; Online gamers notice a delay between pressing a button and the action happening → Latency
